record.original_question: For ideal incompressible Euler flows, are particle trajectories analytic functions of time in all spatial dimensions, and for manifolds with boundary how does this time-analyticity depend on whether the boundary is analytic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an ideal incompressible fluid governed by the Euler equations
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = −∇p,   div u = 0,
on a smooth Riemannian manifold M (possibly with boundary), with the impermeability condition u·ν = 0 on ∂M when ∂M ≠ ∅. For a sufficiently regular initial velocity field u_0, let X(t,a) denote the Lagrangian flow, i.e. the solution of
  d/dt X(t,a) = u(t, X(t,a)),   X(0,a) = a,
for a ∈ M, defined on the maximal interval of existence of the Euler solution.

(a) Is it true that for every spatial dimension n ≥ 2, and for every fluid particle a ∈ M, the map t ↦ X(t,a) is a real-analytic function of time on the interval of existence of a sufficiently regular Eulerian solution, even when the Eulerian velocity field u(·,·) is merely of finite (e.g. Hölder or Sobolev) spatial regularity?

(b) If M has nonempty boundary ∂M, how does the time-analyticity of the Lagrangian trajectories X(t,a) (including for particles on or approaching the boundary) depend on the regularity of ∂M, in particular on whether ∂M is real-analytic versus only smooth or of Gevrey class?
artifact.status_search_result: Time-analyticity of Lagrangian particle trajectories for the incompressible Euler equations has been established in considerable generality on R^n and on the torus by Shnirelman, Frisch–Zheligovsky, Constantin–Vicol–Wu, and others, using a Cauchy-type Lagrangian formulation. For domains with boundary, Gevrey-class regularity up to the boundary has been proved when the boundary is itself of Gevrey class (Kukavica–Vicol and others), but the precise dependence of full time-analyticity of trajectories on the analyticity of the boundary remains delicate and not fully settled in the most general settings. Thus the question is partially solved: the interior/whole-space case is essentially resolved, while the boundary-dependence aspect is only partly understood.

status_evidence.title: Time-analyticity of Lagrangian particle trajectories in ideal fluid flow
status_evidence.snippet: Ideal flow with limited spatial smoothness nevertheless has time-analytic Lagrangian trajectories before the initial limited smoothness is lost.
status_evidence.claim: Time-analyticity of Lagrangian trajectories established for Euler flows with limited Eulerian spatial regularity.

status_evidence.title: On the Analyticity of Particle Trajectories in the Ideal Incompressible Fluid (Shnirelman)
status_evidence.snippet: Analyticity of Lagrangian trajectories for well posed inviscid incompressible fluid models.
status_evidence.claim: Analyticity of particle trajectories is known for well-posed inviscid incompressible models in n dimensions.

status_evidence.title: On the analyticity and Gevrey class regularity up to the boundary for the Euler Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Euler equations in a three-dimensional Gevrey-class bounded domain — Gevrey-class persistence up to the boundary with explicit decay of the Gevrey radius.
status_evidence.claim: For domains with Gevrey-class boundary, Gevrey persistence up to the boundary is proved, indicating that boundary regularity controls trajectory regularity.
